title: Abbotsford Police in-custody death ruled accidental
article: Abbotsford Police Chief Bob Rich said the department will review recommendations made by a jury at a coroner's inquest this week to see if adjustments can be made to the handling of intoxicated prisoners.
The jury ruled that the August 2008 death of Christine Bernadette Miller, 39, was accidental. She had been in medical distress while in police custody and was taken to hospital, where she died.

The inquest took place Tuesday to Thursday at the Coroners Court in Burnaby.The jury ruled that Miller died from a combination of drugs - codeine, acetaminophen, ethanol, diphenhdyramine and diazepam.

Among the six recommendations made by the jury were three for the Abbotsford Police: that a more intensive training program be developed for prisoner searches, that prisoners be roused every two hours when they are known or are suspected to have ingested drugs and/or alcohol, and that guards check prisoners and record their physical state every 15 minutes.
Rich said the department already does a variation of these steps, but the jury's recommendations are more detailed.
For example, he said prisoners are already checked every 15 minutes, but their physical state is not recorded, nor do officers enter their cells and physically rouse them.
Rich said the suggestions will be taken seriously. Miller was in police custody because she was intoxicated and there were concerns about her safety.
"The tragedy here is that when we take someone into custody for this purpose, our goal is to look after them ... In this instance, we failed in that response."
Deputy Chief Rick Lucy gave testimony at the inquest and apologized to Miller's family on behalf of the Abbotsford Police Department.

Rich said the department made some changes immediately following Miller's death, including to fine-tune its policies on strip searches and to assign a sergeant who is solely responsible for the police lock-up.
Another recommendation from the jury was that Fraser Health and the City of Abbotsford establish a "sobering centre" as an alternative to hospital or jail.

The final two were directed to the Minister of Health: to mandate that all doctors in B.C. have on-site access to PharmaNet records and a public awareness campaign be created to educate about the "lethal combination of prescription drugs."
